decisions: The refuter's overturn is upheld and is the whole diagnosis. Caller-side stack-argument recovery is NOT defeated on the witness: with a prototype declared, the same loop-carried esp accesses yield ptrace(v18[-0xc],v18[-0xb],(void *)v18[-10],(void *)v18[-9]) at every one of the 13 sites. Nothing in stack-arg recovery or the esp/alignment model was touched.

The refuter's prescription ('a name-to-signature libc table is what flips this acceptance') needed one correction: kuna ALREADY has two such tables (libproto's 27 entries, libcsigs' ~200). What it does not have is a way for a name that is not in the object to reach them. `present_function_names` unions the FUNC symbols with the import resolver, and this image is stripped, statically linked and has no section header table, so the name exists only because --define-function supplied it. The gap is the LOOKUP SEAM, not the table -- plus one missing row.

Parked by ADDRESS (set_function_prototype_pieces_at), not by name. ActionDefaultParams reads a callee prototype by entry address, and the by-name park queries the global scope only, which answers with the wrong symbol whenever two share a spelling (an import thunk and its IAT slot -- the defect PR #470 half-fixed). --define-function hands us the address outright, so there is no reason to route through a name query.

Both tables are searched from the declared-name seam, libcsigs' imports-only restriction included. That restriction is about a COINCIDENTAL spelling retyping a function the image defines itself; an operator who declared the entry is not a coincidence. Recorded as a deliberate lift, not an oversight.

ptrace went into the BASE table rather than the measured extension: the extension's membership rule is a measured frequency bar over the decbench C corpus and ptrace clears neither (0 of 1709 decbench ELFs carry the symbol at all), so adding it there would contradict that module's stated selection rule. The base table is the one whose documented job is 'common libc signatures, conservative and correct', and it already grew this way once (setlocale, docs/features/setlocale-rettype).

The 4-slot signature is not written from memory, which this module forbids: glibc DECLARES `long ptrace(enum __ptrace_request, ...)` and its own wrapper (sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/ptrace.c) fetches pid_t, void *, void * after the request with va_arg. Those three plus the request are the four slots, and every one is width-stable on ILP32 and LP64.

The declaration seam runs BEFORE the assertion plane (the generated console script emits `function bounds` then `map prototype`), so an explicit --assert prototype on the same function still wins -- verified: `--assert 'prototype ptrace int ptrace(int a)'` renders ptrace(0) on the witness.

Not a tooling-track change despite living in kuna-console: it moves emitted C, so it ships behind a phases.toml option with a DIV row. Default ON because the acceptance probe passes no --option, and because the flip is structurally inert without a declaration.

A stages XML IS possible here, contrary to the usual analysis-tier rule: `function bounds ... as NAME` is a console command and the XML `<com>` plane reaches it over a plain <bytechunk>, no object file needed. The two-pass case is therefore a real gate test, not just a cargo test.
